skill.name: yescan-transoffice-universal
skill.description: Convert one user-provided image, screenshot, or scan into an editable Word, Excel, or PDF file through Quark Scan King. The skill accepts URL, local path, or base64 input.
skill.summary: Convert a single image, screenshot, or scan into Word, Excel, or PDF using Quark Scan King.
skill.author: yescan-ai

security_audit.summary: Review confirmed expected but material risks: the skill uploads user images or file-derived base64 plus SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY to a hard-coded Quark endpoint, then saves returned documents under the system temp directory. Many static hits are documentation or syntax false positives, but real issues remain around third-party data transfer, plaintext key-file fallback, prompt instructions that can ignore prior context, and shell command templates using user-controlled placeholders.

remediation.issue: Prompt instructions tell the agent not to use prior conversation context.
remediation.suggestion: Remove language that forbids using conversation history, and state that higher-priority system and user instructions always apply.

remediation.issue: Command templates rely on direct substitution of user-provided URL, path, or base64 values.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to invoke the script through argv-safe execution and never through shell string interpolation.

remediation.issue: API key can be stored in plaintext at ~/.yescan_env.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the agent secret store or OS credential manager, enforce file permissions, and document rotation after suspected exposure.

remediation.issue: User images and API keys are sent to a third-party conversion service.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user consent before processing sensitive documents and show the exact destination service.

remediation.issue: Converted documents are saved in the system temp directory and are not auto-cleaned.
remediation.suggestion: Add cleanup guidance in the runtime response or support a user-selected output directory with retention controls.

remediation.issue: Returned Office and PDF content is saved without document magic-byte validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate file signatures for generated documents and warn users before opening files returned by the service.

content.value_statement: Scanned images often need retyping before they can be edited or archived. This skill sends one image to Quark Scan King and returns a Word, Excel, or PDF file path.
actual_capabilities: Converts one image into Word, Excel, or PDF through Quark Scan King.
Accepts image input as a URL, local file path, or base64 string.
Validates local image extension and size before upload.
Loads SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY from the environment or a local config file.
Saves converted documents to the system temp directory and returns the path.
limitations: Requires network access to the Quark Scan King API.
Requires a SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY API key before use.
Supports one image per request with a 5 MB local file limit.
Does not perform pure text extraction, image enhancement, or new document authoring.

use_cases.title: Convert Meeting Notes
use_cases.description: Turn a photo of notes into an editable Word document for cleanup and sharing.

use_cases.title: Recover Table Data
use_cases.description: Convert a screenshot of a table or report into an Excel workbook for review.

use_cases.title: Archive Scanned Records
use_cases.description: Create a PDF from a scanned image while preserving the visible page layout.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Photo to Word
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a local image file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this photo to a Word document: /path/to/meeting-notes.jpg

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Table to Excel
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using an image URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this table screenshot to Excel: https://example.com/report.png

prompt_templates.title: Create a PDF Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this scanned contract image to PDF and return the saved file path.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request where the user describes the document goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: This image contains a mixed layout with signatures and stamps. Convert it to the best supported Office or PDF format.

output_examples.input: A user provides a local photo of handwritten meeting notes.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a saved Word document path that the user can open and edit.

output_examples.input: A user provides a URL to a screenshot of a financial table.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a saved Excel workbook path for spreadsheet review.

output_examples.input: A user provides a scan of a signed contract page.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a saved PDF path that preserves the page layout.

best_practices: Confirm user consent before sending sensitive images to a third-party service.
Use clear, upright images with visible text and table borders.
Delete converted temp files after they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for batch conversion without user confirmation.
Do not upload regulated or confidential images without approval.
Do not use it when the user only wants plain text extraction.

faq.question: Does this skill process images locally?
faq.answer: No. It sends the image or image URL to Quark Scan King for conversion.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Word, Excel, and PDF output for single image inputs.

faq.question: Where are converted files saved?
faq.answer: Converted files are saved in the system temp directory and returned as a file path.

faq.question: What API key is required?
faq.answer: The skill requires SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY in the environment or the configured local key file.

faq.question: Can it process multiple images at once?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow supports one image per request.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive documents?
faq.answer: Use caution. Sensitive images leave the machine and are processed by a third-party service.
